subject: Configuring shared and distinct hyperparameters for two spatial fields

messages.author: 17f8070912132195
messages.subject: Configuring shared and distinct hyperparameters for two spatial fields
parts:
Dear INLA group,

I am working on a hurdle model defined as follows:

aniso.model <- inla.aniso.pcmatern(mesh,
                                   prior.range = c(diff(range(mesh$loc[, 1])) / 5, 0.5),
                                   prior.sigma = c(1, 0.5),
                                   prior.h1 = c(0, 1),
                                   prior.h2 = c(0, 1))

form <- y ~ -1 + z.b0 + y.b0 +

  f(ves.z, model="iid", hyper=list(theta=list(param=c(0.1,0.1))), constr=TRUE) +
  f(yq.z, model="rw1", hyper=list(theta=list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(0.5,0.01))), scale.model=TRUE, constr=TRUE) +
  f(sz, model=aniso.model) +
 
  f(ves.y, model="iid", hyper=list(theta=list(param=c(0.1,0.1))), constr=TRUE) +
  f(yq.y, model="rw1", hyper=list(theta=list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(0.5,0.01))), scale.model=TRUE, constr=TRUE) +
  f(sy, model=aniso.model)

I would like sz and sy to share the same h1 and h2 values but have different range and sigma parameters. I’m wondering if there is a simple command, like "fixed xx," that could achieve this.

Thanks,
Ruby

Hi Håvard,

Thank you for your guidance. I defined a new rgeneric model that includes two fields with six hyperparameters (h1, h2, two ranges, and two sigmas). The precision matrix, Q, is formed using bdiag, which combines two matrices Qz​ and Qy​ along the main diagonal while filling other positions with zeros. Thus, the dimension of the new Q is (2×mesh$n)×(2×mesh$n). The dimension of the A matrix remains nobs​×mesh$n. To operate only one field in each sub-model, I adjusted the spatial index for sy​ accordingly.

I'd like to confirm if what I did is correct. I really appreciate your comments!


The INLA model was defined as:
# A matrix
A <- inla.spde.make.A(
  mesh = mesh,
  loc = as.matrix(dat[, c("X", "Y")])
)

# Index
indz <- inla.spde.make.index(name = "sz", n.spde = mesh$n)
indy <- inla.spde.make.index(name = "sy", n.spde = mesh$n)
indy$sy <- indy$sy + mesh$n      # Is it correct here?

# Stack data
stk.z <- inla.stack(tag='est.z',
                    data=list(y=cbind(as.vector(z), NA), link=1),
                              A=list(A, 1),
                              effects=list(indz,
                                           list(z.b0=rep(1,length(z)),
                                                yq.z=dat$yq,
                                                ves.z=dat$vesno)))

stk.y <- inla.stack(tag='est.y',
                       data=list(y=cbind(NA, as.vector(y)), link=2),
                       A=list(A, 1),
                       effects=list(indy,
                                    list(y.b0=rep(1,length(y)),
                                         yq.y=dat$yq,
                                         ves.y=dat$vesno)))

stk.all <- inla.stack(stk.z, stk.y)


# INLA formula

form <- y ~ -1 + z.b0 + y.b0 +
  f(ves.z, model="iid", hyper=list(theta=list(param=c(0.1,0.1))), constr=TRUE) +
  f(yq.z, model="rw1", hyper=list(theta=list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(0.5,0.01))), scale.model=TRUE, constr=TRUE) +
  f(sz, model=aniso.model) +
  f(ves.y, model="iid", hyper=list(theta=list(param=c(0.1,0.1))), constr=TRUE) +
  f(yq.y, model="rw1", hyper=list(theta=list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(0.5,0.01))), scale.model=TRUE, constr=TRUE) +

f(sy, copy="sz", fixed=TRUE)     #Copy here

Thanks,
Ruby
